fields.text: A picture passed hand to hand until only words carry it. A GLM director writes a SCENE CARD of exactly 6 numbered elements, a second GLM turns it into a painter prompt, and Muse paints generation 1. Then the relay starts: a blind Gemini reader inventories generation 1 and writes a recreation prompt; a GLM relay clerk extracts that prompt verbatim; Muse paints generation 2 from those words alone - it never sees generation 1. A second reader and clerk pass it on to generation 3 the same way. A GLM drift auditor scores how many of the card's 6 elements survive at EACH hop, which hop each loss happened at, and what the chain invented along the way. A Decide judge gives the headline on the trajectory: survived the relay, drifted slowly, collapsed mid-relay, or mutated beyond recognition. See recipes/relay-drift.md.

nodes.name: Relay drift, hop-checked - one scene, three generations, only words pass between them

fields.text: A small harbour cafe terrace at sunrise, seen from the water side.

fields.system:
You are a scene director. Given a SEED scene, write a SCENE CARD with exactly 6 numbered ELEMENTS that a painter can draw and a reader can check. Each element is ONE concrete visible thing with a specific colour, count or position (for example 'a red fishing boat tied at the left edge', 'three white seagulls on the roof ridge'). Elements must be distinct, non-overlapping, and likely to survive being described in words. Output exactly this shape and nothing else:
SETTING: <the seed scene in a few words>
STYLE: photorealistic, warm sunrise light, no text
ELEMENTS:
1. <element>
2. <element>
3. <element>
4. <element>
5. <element>
6. <element>

fields.system: You turn a SCENE CARD into ONE prompt for an AI image generator. The input gives a SEED first, then 'SCENE CARD' with a SETTING, a STYLE line and 6 numbered ELEMENTS. Write a single vivid prompt that paints the setting in that style and includes every one of the 6 elements exactly as described - same colours, counts and positions. End with: 'Photorealistic, warm sunrise light, no text, no letters, no people close to the camera.' Output the prompt only.

fields.q:
You are a relay reader in a serial-reproduction pipeline. You see one picture. First inventory ONLY what is actually visible, then write a recreation prompt good enough for another painter to recreate this picture from your words alone - that painter will never see the picture, only your prompt. Output exactly this shape and nothing else:
INVENTORY:
1. <one visible element per line, with colour, count and position; list every distinct element you can see, at most 10>
RECREATION PROMPT:
<one paragraph, at most 120 words, describing the whole picture - setting, style, light, and every inventoried element with its colour, count and position; end with 'Photorealistic, warm sunrise light, no text.'>

fields.system:
You are a drift auditor. The input gives a SCENE CARD (SETTING, STYLE and 6 numbered ELEMENTS), then GEN 1, GEN 2 and GEN 3 READER REPORTS, each with an INVENTORY section. Compare ONLY the INVENTORY sections against the card's 6 elements. An element SURVIVES a generation if the inventory names the same thing with the same colour, count and position (near wording counts; a changed colour, count or position is a loss). Output exactly these lines:
HOP 1: <X> of 6
HOP 2: <X> of 6
HOP 3: <X> of 6
LOST AT HOP 1: <card element numbers lost in generation 1, or 'none'>
LOST AT HOP 2: <card element numbers first lost in generation 2, or 'none'>
LOST AT HOP 3: <card element numbers first lost in generation 3, or 'none'>
INVENTED: <elements appearing in any inventory that are not on the card, comma-separated, or 'none'>
Summary: hop 1 <X> of 6, hop 2 <X> of 6, hop 3 <X> of 6.
If any report is incomplete, still output all lines with your best judgement and say 'incomplete report' in the Summary. Never output nothing. Compare only the texts; do not invent readings. Output the audit only.

nodes.name: Drift audit - GLM scores element survival at each hop

fields.question: A scene was painted, described in words by a blind reader, repainted from those words alone, described again and repainted a third time - a serial reproduction relay. The text gives the original SCENE CARD (6 planned elements), the three generations' reader inventories, and a DRIFT AUDIT scoring how many card elements survive at each hop and what was invented along the way. Which verdict fits the trajectory? 'survived the relay' means hop 3 still keeps 5 or 6 of 6 elements. 'drifted slowly' means elements were lost gradually, hop 3 keeping 3 or 4 of 6. 'collapsed mid-relay' means one single hop lost 3 or more elements. 'mutated beyond recognition' means hop 3 keeps 2 or fewer of 6, or the inventions outnumber the survivors. Judge the trajectory in the audit, not the final picture's beauty.
fields.options:
survived the relay
drifted slowly
collapsed mid-relay
mutated beyond recognition
